best_for: People with a home theater PC or a computer by the TV who want to browse their own movies, shows and music from the couch with a remote.

points.title: Made for the couch
points.text: Kodi's interface is designed to be read from across the room and driven with a remote, not a mouse.

points.title: Your files, with posters
points.text: Kodi scans your media and builds a library with cover art, descriptions and fanart. It plays files from local drives, network shares and internet streams.

points.title: Bring your own content
points.text: Kodi plays and organizes media you point it to; it is a player, not a streaming service. Extra features come from add-ons, mostly written in Python.

points.title: Free, run by volunteers
points.text: Kodi is open source under the GPL and maintained by volunteers through the non-profit XBMC Foundation. It also runs on Android, iOS, tvOS and BSD.

points.title: Windows keeps older releases
points.text: The Windows installers, 32-bit and 64-bit, install per-user. The Windows listing keeps 24 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.

points.title: Linux Flatpak from Team Kodi
points.text: The Flathub build is published by Team Kodi, for x64 and Arm64, and is about 300 MB to download. Mac builds come for Intel and Apple Silicon.
